title: Token signal reconciliation pipeline for cost telemetry and KV-prefetch crediting
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reconciliation pipeline that ingests per-token timing signals, cache hit/miss indicators and frontend emission metadata to produce a reconciled, auditable cost telemetry stream. This ticket covers schema design, ingestion hooks (tracing + metrics), offline join logic to attribute KV-prefetch savings to specific emission slices, and the initial dashboards and alerts needed for QA and rollout. Goal: provide token-level cost signals that account for prefetch credits and avoid double-counting when requests use multiple cache layers.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation hooks added to serving runtime to emit token-level events (token_id, request_id, timestamp_ns, stage, kv_hit:boolean, prefetch_budget_used:int)
A reconciler job that consumes event_stream -> joins with request metadata -> emits token_cost_line for billing pipeline with stable request and token identifiers
Unit and integration tests that validate attribution across synthetic cases: full cache hit, partial prefetch consumption, fallback model variant
Dashboard showing token-level latency distribution, percent of prefetch credits applied, and top 10 request patterns causing largest billing discrepancies
Migration plan and rollout gating: feature flag for emitters, opt-in region, and canary on 5% of traffic before full rollout
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava: Scoped initial schema, decided on compact event format with stable token_id and request_id. Will use 64-bit ns timestamps to avoid jitter from clock sync.
2025-02-22 - Liam: Implemented emitter prototype in runtime: emits token.events to Kafka topic 'token-signals.v1'. Local integration tests pass for single-request flows.
2025-02-25 - Design review (Maya): Asked to include 'prefetch_origin' attribute (local-batch vs remote-predictor) and a 'kv_ttl' field for downstream heuristics. Added to schema.

2025-03-03 - QA: Found duplicate token events when runtime admitted retry flows; added idempotency logic using request_id + token_index to reconciler join stage.
2025-03-05 - Liam: Reconciler job v0 landed to staging (PR #219). Next: add sampling configuration and end-to-end billing pipeline connect.
Notes: Link to incident learning doc for similar double-counting issue: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV+double+counting+postmortem
decisions: Use event-first architecture: emit minimal token events from runtime to Kafka and perform enrichment in the reconciler rather than bloating runtime payloads.
Apply sampling on high-volume models at emitter level (configurable per-model) and perform probabilistic upscaling in reconciler to estimate total cost.
Represent prefetch crediting as a separate refundable field on token_cost_line rather than adjusting base token cost to keep bills auditable.
Do not ship raw logits or model internals in token events; use fingerprint field for correlation instead.
Use feature-flagged rollout and a canary at 5% traffic before enabling reconciler for all accounts.
risks: High cardinality of token events could overwhelm Kafka if un-sampled for large models; mitigated by per-model sampling and batching emitters.
Incorrect join logic could under/over-credit prefetch budgets leading to customer billing discrepancies; require synthetic regression suite.
Clock skew between shards could mis-order events; use ns timestamp + ordering window in reconciler and tolerate small reordering by buffering.
Privacy/compliance constraints prevent shipping certain model signals; design avoids raw logits and includes hashed fingerprints instead.
test_plan: Unit tests for emitter: validate schema, required fields, and behavior under retry
Integration test: start local Kafka, run runtime emitter against reconciler, assert token_cost_lines match golden dataset for five synthetic scenarios
Load test: simulate 10k req/s with realistic token distributions to validate Kafka throughput and reconciler latency
Canary: enable on staging -> 5% production traffic -> compare reconciled cost to baseline for drift <0.5% before 100% rollout
